description: Enterprise. Compares ways to move a heavy load to a Texas site from an origin (default the nearest port; or a Texas town, address or point): (1) truck direct on the truck router, (2) truck to the nearest active rail line, rail on the FRA North American Rail Network to the rail-served transload or intermodal terminal nearest the site, then truck to the site. Gives miles per leg, railroads on the rail leg and how many times the line changes railroad, and an indicative linehaul cost per option from published national averages (BTS NTS Table 3-21 revenue per ton-mile: truck 27.07 cents 2022, Class I rail 5.19 cents 2023; ATRI 2025 truck operating cost $2.336 per mile). The averages are general freight, not oversize permit loads, and exclude transload handling, switching, permits, escorts and rigging, so use them to rank options, not to budget. (3) truck to the nearest dock, barge on the Gulf Intracoastal Waterway, ship channels and connected rivers to the dock nearest the site, then truck (BTS domestic water 3.84 cents per ton-mile, 2022). Docks are USACE navigation units; confirm one handles project cargo. Run heavy_haul on the truck legs for bridges and low-water crossings.

address.description: Texas street address, e.g. '1201 Main St, Houston, TX'. Use this or lat/lng.

lat.description: Latitude (WGS84). Use with lng instead of address.

lng.description: Longitude (WGS84). Use with lat instead of address.

origin.description: nearest_port (default), or a Texas address or town the load ships from.

origin_lat.description: Origin latitude (with origin_lng) instead of origin.

weight_tons.description: Payload in US tons to move. Default 100.

name: haul_compare
title: Haul options: truck direct vs rail then truck, with indicative costs
